descriptionChirho: A physical bond, chain, or fetter used for imprisonment or restraint. The majority of NT occurrences (Lk 8:29; Acts 16:26, 20:23, 23:29, 26:29, 26:31; Phil 1:7, 13, 14, 17; Col 4:18; 2 Tim 2:9; Phlm 10, 13; Heb 11:36; Jude 6) denote literal chains and fetters of incarceration. Cross-linguistic translations uniformly use bondage/chain vocabulary: arb quyud (chains/fetters), deu Fesseln (fetters), fra lien/chaines (bonds/chains), heb kevalim/moserot (fetters/bonds), hin bandhan/bediyan (bonds/shackles), kor gyeolbak/soesaseul (binding/chains), spa cadenas/ataduras (chains/bonds). Paul's imprisonment bonds (Phil, Col, Phlm, 2 Tim) and the eschatological bonds of Jude 6 (angels kept in bonds) all belong to this concrete restraint sense.

A figurative bond or binding constraint on a person's faculty or condition, used metaphorically for affliction or disability rather than literal incarceration. In Mk 7:35 the 'bond of his tongue' (desmos tes glosses) refers to the speech impediment that was loosed at Jesus's healing, and in Lk 13:16 Satan's 'bond' on the crippled woman for eighteen years denotes spiritual/physical oppression. Hebrew translations use qesher (knot/bond) and khevel (cord/fetter) rather than the imprisonment-specific kevalim, and Arabic uses ribat (band/ligature) rather than quyud (chains), confirming a distinct semantic profile from the imprisonment sense. Both occurrences involve liberation from a constraining condition through divine healing.
